Determine whether the following signal is periodic- if periodic ,determine the fundamental period.

$x(t)=\cos(2t)+\sin(3t).$

For each of the following continuous-time systems, analyze and state whether the system is linear, has memory, and is causal.

a) $y(t)=\dfrac{1}{t}x(t)$

b) $y(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}x(\tau)\,dt$

questions.markdown:
Find Z-transform of the following signal and plot poles, zeros and RoC

$$
x[n]=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^n u[-n]
$$

Draw direct form I implementation of the system-

$$
y(t)+3\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=2x(t)+4\frac{dx(t)}{dt}
$$

Determine the DTFT of the signal,

$$
x[n]=n\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n u[n-3]
$$

Consider a Discrete Time signal

$$
x[n]=u[n+3]-2u[n]+u[n-4]u[n+3].
$$

Sketch

a) $x[n]$

b) $x[2n-3]$

c) $-x[3-n]$
Illustrate the product and shifting property of discrete impulse function.

For each impulse response, determine whether the corresponding LTI system is

(i) Memory less

(ii) Causal

(iii) Stable

$$
h_1[n]=(0.8)^{|n|}\ \text{and}\ h_2[n]=(0.7)^n u[n]-(0.7)^{n-4}u[n-4]
$$

Draw direct form I and direct form II implementations for the following difference equation

$$
y[n]+\frac{1}{2}y[n-1]-y[n-3]=3x[n-1]+2x[n-2]
$$

Evaluate the discrete-time convolution sum

$$
y[n]=u[n]*u[n-3]
$$

For each of the following signals, sampled with sampling interval $T_S$, determine the bounds on $T_S$, which guarantee that there will be no aliasing:

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{t}\sin(3\pi t)+\cos(3\pi t)
$$
